title: Llist 헤더 전체: 동시 실행 표와 분리 후 순회
area: 연결 리스트 · 원자 연산 · ABA · 소유권
guide: 헤드에는 first 하나, 노드에는 next 하나만 있는 NULL 종료 단방향 줄입니다. 보통 공유 줄에서 분리한 뒤에 순회합니다.
노드의 off-list 표시는 next가 자기 자신인 상태입니다. NULL은 정상 줄의 마지막에도 쓰므로 분리 표지와 같지 않습니다.
safe 순회는 다음 노드를 미리 저장해 현재 것을 정리하기 쉽게 할 뿐, 공유 줄을 아무렇게나 동시에 수정해도 된다는 허락은 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 전체 구성과 동시 조합
deep_dive.text: GPL-2.0-only와 보호 조건 뒤 설명 표는 add/add, add/del_first, add/del_all, del_all/del_all을 잠금 없는 조합으로 둡니다. del_first끼리와 del_first/del_all에는 잠금이 필요합니다. 이어 원자 연산·container_of·크기·타입 헤더, 구조와 초기화·순회·조회·추가·삭제 및 외부 선언이 나옵니다.

deep_dive.title: 헤드와 노드 초기화는 다르다
deep_dive.text: 헤드 선언 매크로와 init_llist_head는 first=NULL입니다. init_llist_node는 next=자기 자신으로 분리 표지를 만듭니다. 마지막 노드 next=NULL과 구별하려는 것입니다. 단순 헤드 초기화는 공유 줄을 원자적으로 가져오는 삭제와 다릅니다.

deep_dive.title: on_list가 검사하는 실제 식
deep_dive.text: on_list는 next!=자기 자신만 봅니다. 삭제 함수가 항상 노드 표지를 바꾸지는 않아 분리된 뒤도 참일 수 있습니다. del_first_init은 성공 노드를 초기화해 표지를 복원합니다. 어느 헤드에 속하는지나 다른 CPU의 사용 여부를 검색하는 함수가 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 안쪽 노드로 바깥 객체 찾기
deep_dive.text: llist_entry는 container_of입니다. NULL 노드로 계산한 바깥 포인터는 멤버 위치 때문에 단순 NULL이 아닐 수 있어 member_address_is_nonnull을 씁니다. 주소 숫자에 offsetof를 더해 멤버 주소가 0인지 확인합니다. 없는 객체를 일반적으로 역참조해도 된다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 네 가지 순회 도구
deep_dive.text: for_each는 next를 따라가고 safe는 다음 노드를 n에 저장합니다. entry와 entry_safe는 안쪽 연결 멤버로 바깥 객체를 얻어 같은 일을 합니다. 원문은 일반적으로 먼저 분리한 줄에서 시작하라고 합니다. safe는 현재 항목 삭제를 돕지 공유 중인 활성 체인의 모든 경쟁을 해결하지 않습니다.

deep_dive.title: 빈 줄 검사의 순간성
deep_dive.text: empty는 READ_ONCE(first)==NULL의 빠른 관측입니다. 최신 정확 상태가 보장되지 않으며 바로 뒤 다른 생산자가 넣을 수 있습니다. next 도우미도 단순 필드 읽기라 독립적인 동기화나 노드 수명 보호를 주지 않습니다.

deep_dive.title: 일반 삽입과 두 밑줄 삽입
deep_dive.text: llist_add는 같은 노드를 외부 원자 add_batch의 처음·끝으로 넘깁니다. __llist_add_batch는 꼬리와 헤드를 일반 대입으로 잇고 __llist_add가 이를 씁니다. 두 밑줄 버전에는 CAS가 없어 단독 접근이나 외부 잠금 등 별도 보호가 필요합니다.

deep_dive.title: 전체 줄 가져오기
deep_dive.text: del_all은 xchg로 first를 NULL로 원자 교환하여 이전 줄을 반환합니다. __del_all은 일반 읽기·쓰기뿐입니다. 둘 다 노드를 free하지 않습니다. 하나씩 앞에 넣었다면 최신 노드부터 나오며 reverse로 뒤집을 수 있습니다. 묶음 내부는 생산자가 연결한 순서입니다.

deep_dive.title: 단일 삭제와 표지 복원
deep_dive.text: del_first는 외부 선언이고 del_first_init은 결과가 있으면 init_llist_node를 부릅니다. 지정 첫 삭제와 역순 함수도 외부 선언입니다. 문서의 llist_init_node라는 철자와 실제 호출 init_llist_node를 구별하여 실행 코드를 기준으로 봅니다.

deep_dive.title: 동기화 범위와 핵심 개념
deep_dive.text: 원자 교환은 값을 통째로 바꾸고 CAS는 예상값 확인 후 바꿉니다. 객체 안에 연결 멤버를 넣는 구조와 분리한 작업 묶음의 처리가 핵심입니다. NMI에서는 안전한 cmpxchg 지원 조건이 필요합니다. lock-less, 즉 특정 잠금 없이 동작한다는 말이 모든 실행 환경에서 재시도 없이 끝나는 wait-free를 보장하지는 않습니다.

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only */
#ifndef LLIST_H
#define LLIST_H
/*
 * Lock-less NULL terminated single linked list
 *
 * Cases where locking is not needed:
 * If there are multiple producers and multiple consumers, llist_add can be
 * used in producers and llist_del_all can be used in consumers simultaneously
 * without locking. Also a single consumer can use llist_del_first while
 * multiple producers simultaneously use llist_add, without any locking.
 *
 * Cases where locking is needed:
 * If we have multiple consumers with llist_del_first used in one consumer, and
 * llist_del_first or llist_del_all used in other consumers, then a lock is
 * needed.  This is because llist_del_first depends on list->first->next not
 * changing, but without lock protection, there's no way to be sure about that
 * if a preemption happens in the middle of the delete operation and on being
 * preempted back, the list->first is the same as before causing the cmpxchg in
 * llist_del_first to succeed. For example, while a llist_del_first operation
 * is in progress in one consumer, then a llist_del_first, llist_add,
 * llist_add (or llist_del_all, llist_add, llist_add) sequence in another
 * consumer may cause violations.
 *
 * This can be summarized as follows:
 *
 *           |   add    | del_first |  del_all
 * add       |    -     |     -     |     -
 * del_first |          |     L     |     L
 * del_all   |          |           |     -
 *
 * Where, a particular row's operation can happen concurrently with a column's
 * operation, with "-" being no lock needed, while "L" being lock is needed.
 *
 * The list entries deleted via llist_del_all can be traversed with
 * traversing function such as llist_for_each etc.  But the list
 * entries can not be traversed safely before deleted from the list.
 * The order of deleted entries is from the newest to the oldest added
 * one.  If you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you
 * must reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 *
 * The basic atomic operation of this list is cmpxchg on long.  On
 * architectures that don't have NMI-safe cmpxchg implementation, the
 * list can NOT be used in NMI handlers.  So code that uses the list in
 * an NMI handler should depend on CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_NMI_SAFE_CMPXCHG.
 *
 * Copyright 2010,2011 Intel Corp.
 *   Author: Huang Ying <ying.huang@intel.com>
 */

#include <linux/atomic.h>
#include <linux/container_of.h>
#include <linux/stddef.h>
#include <linux/types.h>

struct llist_head {
	struct llist_node *first;
};

struct llist_node {
	struct llist_node *next;
};

#define LLIST_HEAD_INIT(name)	{ NULL }
#define LLIST_HEAD(name)	struct llist_head name = LLIST_HEAD_INIT(name)

/**
 * init_llist_head - initialize lock-less list head
 * @head:	the head for your lock-less list
 */
static inline void init_llist_head(struct llist_head *list)
{
	list->first = NULL;
}

/**
 * init_llist_node - initialize lock-less list node
 * @node:	the node to be initialised
 *
 * In cases where there is a need to test if a node is on
 * a list or not, this initialises the node to clearly
 * not be on any list.
 */
static inline void init_llist_node(struct llist_node *node)
{
	node->next = node;
}

/**
 * llist_on_list - test if a lock-list list node is on a list
 * @node:	the node to test
 *
 * When a node is on a list the ->next pointer will be NULL or
 * some other node.  It can never point to itself.  We use that
 * in init_llist_node() to record that a node is not on any list,
 * and here to test whether it is on any list.
 */
static inline bool llist_on_list(const struct llist_node *node)
{
	return node->next != node;
}

/**
 * llist_entry - get the struct of this entry
 * @ptr:	the &struct llist_node pointer.
 * @type:	the type of the struct this is embedded in.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node within the struct.
 */
#define llist_entry(ptr, type, member)		\
	container_of(ptr, type, member)

/**
 * member_address_is_nonnull - check whether the member address is not NULL
 * @ptr:	the object pointer (struct type * that contains the llist_node)
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node within the struct.
 *
 * This macro is conceptually the same as
 *	&ptr->member != NULL
 * but it works around the fact that compilers can decide that taking a member
 * address is never a NULL pointer.
 *
 * Real objects that start at a high address and have a member at NULL are
 * unlikely to exist, but such pointers may be returned e.g. by the
 * container_of() macro.
 */
#define member_address_is_nonnull(ptr, member)	\
	((uintptr_t)(ptr) + offsetof(typeof(*(ptr)), member) != 0)

/**
 * llist_for_each - iterate over some deleted entries of a lock-less list
 * @pos:	the &struct llist_node to use as a loop cursor
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being deleted from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each(pos, node)			\
	for ((pos) = (node); pos; (pos) = (pos)->next)

/**
 * llist_for_each_safe - iterate over some deleted entries of a lock-less list
 *			 safe against removal of list entry
 * @pos:	the &struct llist_node to use as a loop cursor
 * @n:		another &struct llist_node to use as temporary storage
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being deleted from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_safe(pos, n, node)			\
	for ((pos) = (node); (pos) && ((n) = (pos)->next, true); (pos) = (n))

/**
 * llist_for_each_entry - iterate over some deleted entries of lock-less list of given type
 * @pos:	the type * to use as a loop cursor.
 * @node:	the fist entry of deleted list entries.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node with the struct.
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being removed from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_entry(pos, node, member)				\
	for ((pos) = llist_entry((node), typeof(*(pos)), member);	\
	     member_address_is_nonnull(pos, member);			\
	     (pos) = llist_entry((pos)->member.next, typeof(*(pos)), member))

/**
 * llist_for_each_entry_safe - iterate over some deleted entries of lock-less list of given type
 *			       safe against removal of list entry
 * @pos:	the type * to use as a loop cursor.
 * @n:		another type * to use as temporary storage
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node with the struct.
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being removed from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_entry_safe(pos, n, node, member)			       \
	for (pos = llist_entry((node), typeof(*pos), member);		       \
	     member_address_is_nonnull(pos, member) &&			       \
	        (n = llist_entry(pos->member.next, typeof(*n), member), true); \
	     pos = n)

/**
 * llist_empty - tests whether a lock-less list is empty
 * @head:	the list to test
 *
 * Not guaranteed to be accurate or up to date.  Just a quick way to
 * test whether the list is empty without deleting something from the
 * list.
 */
static inline bool llist_empty(const struct llist_head *head)
{
	return READ_ONCE(head->first) == NULL;
}

static inline struct llist_node *llist_next(struct llist_node *node)
{
	return node->next;
}

extern bool llist_add_batch(struct llist_node *new_first,
			    struct llist_node *new_last,
			    struct llist_head *head);

static inline bool __llist_add_batch(struct llist_node *new_first,
				     struct llist_node *new_last,
				     struct llist_head *head)
{
	new_last->next = head->first;
	head->first = new_first;
	return new_last->next == NULL;
}

/**
 * llist_add - add a new entry
 * @new:	new entry to be added
 * @head:	the head for your lock-less list
 *
 * Returns true if the list was empty prior to adding this entry.
 */
static inline bool llist_add(struct llist_node *new, struct llist_head *head)
{
	return llist_add_batch(new, new, head);
}

static inline bool __llist_add(struct llist_node *new, struct llist_head *head)
{
	return __llist_add_batch(new, new, head);
}

/**
 * llist_del_all - delete all entries from lock-less list
 * @head:	the head of lock-less list to delete all entries
 *
 * If list is empty, return NULL, otherwise, delete all entries and
 * return the pointer to the first entry.  The order of entries
 * deleted is from the newest to the oldest added one.
 */
static inline struct llist_node *llist_del_all(struct llist_head *head)
{
	return xchg(&head->first, NULL);
}

static inline struct llist_node *__llist_del_all(struct llist_head *head)
{
	struct llist_node *first = head->first;

	head->first = NULL;
	return first;
}

extern struct llist_node *llist_del_first(struct llist_head *head);

/**
 * llist_del_first_init - delete first entry from lock-list and mark is as being off-list
 * @head:	the head of lock-less list to delete from.
 *
 * This behave the same as llist_del_first() except that llist_init_node() is called
 * on the returned node so that llist_on_list() will report false for the node.
 */
static inline struct llist_node *llist_del_first_init(struct llist_head *head)
{
	struct llist_node *n = llist_del_first(head);

	if (n)
		init_llist_node(n);
	return n;
}

extern bool llist_del_first_this(struct llist_head *head,
				 struct llist_node *this);

struct llist_node *llist_reverse_order(struct llist_node *head);

#endif /* LLIST_H */

source_review.verification: 파일 전체를 읽고 데이터·정의·선언·메타데이터와 경계 조건을 개별 작성. source_sha256은 원본 동일성을 검사하며 실행 정확성이나 의미 완전성의 자동 증명이 아님.

technical_original.intro: 잠금 없는 단일 리스트의 구조체, 순회 매크로, 원자·비원자 wrapper와 사용 계약을 제공합니다.
guide: 활성 리스트에서 체인을 원자적으로 분리한 뒤 순회하는 모델입니다. 헤드에는 first 하나, 노드에는 next 하나만 들어 있습니다.
순회·삭제·노드 표시의 계약을 각각 확인해야 합니다. llist_on_list는 실제 특정 헤드의 구성원을 검색하는 함수가 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 전체 구성과 동시 실행 표
deep_dive.text: SPDX와 guard 뒤의 긴 주석은 add/add, add/del_first, add/del_all, del_all/del_all은 잠금 없이 가능한 조합으로 설명합니다. del_first/del_first와 del_first/del_all에는 잠금이 필요합니다. 이어 atomic/container_of/stddef/types, 구조체·초기화·순회·조회·삽입·삭제 wrapper와 외부 선언이 있습니다.

deep_dive.title: 헤드와 노드 초기화의 차이
deep_dive.text: LLIST_HEAD_INIT과 LLIST_HEAD, init_llist_head는 헤드를 NULL로 초기화합니다. init_llist_node는 next를 자기 자신으로 설정해 off-list 표식을 만듭니다. 정상 체인의 마지막 노드는 next=NULL이므로 NULL을 off-list 표식으로 사용할 수 없습니다. 헤드 초기화는 공유 중인 데이터를 안전하게 비우는 원자 삭제와 다릅니다.

deep_dive.title: on_list의 실제 의미
deep_dive.text: llist_on_list는 node->next!=node만 검사합니다. 삭제 함수가 항상 이 표식을 복구하는 것은 아니므로 분리되었어도 true일 수 있습니다. del_first_init은 삭제 성공 시 init_llist_node를 호출해 표식을 복구합니다. 어느 헤드에 있는지, 현재 다른 CPU가 접근하는지까지 판정하지 않습니다.

deep_dive.title: 객체 복원과 NULL 경계
deep_dive.text: llist_entry는 container_of입니다. entry 순회에서 NULL 노드를 감싼 계산상의 객체 포인터가 단순 NULL이 아닐 수 있어 member_address_is_nonnull을 사용합니다. 이 매크로는 uintptr_t 주소에 offsetof를 더해 멤버 주소가0인지 검사합니다. 실제 존재하지 않는 객체를 일반적으로 역참조해도 된다는 뜻이 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 네 순회 매크로
deep_dive.text: llist_for_each는 노드 next를 따라가고 safe는 다음 노드를 임시 n에 저장합니다. entry와 entry_safe는 포함 객체 타입과 member를 사용해 같은 역할을 합니다. 문서는 일반적으로 리스트에서 삭제·분리한 노드부터 순회하라고 요구합니다. safe는 현재 항목 정리를 돕는 것으로 활성 공유 체인의 임의 동시 수정 허가가 아닙니다.

deep_dive.title: 빈 리스트 검사와 next
deep_dive.text: llist_empty는 READ_ONCE(head->first)==NULL이며 문서가 최신·정확 상태를 보장하지 않는 빠른 검사라고 명시합니다. 검사 다음 순간 다른 생산자가 삽입할 수 있습니다. llist_next는 단순 next 읽기이며 독립적인 동기화나 수명 보호를 제공하지 않습니다.

deep_dive.title: 삽입 wrapper와 이중 밑줄
deep_dive.text: llist_add는 외부 llist_add_batch에 new를 first/last로 전달합니다. __llist_add_batch는 꼬리와 헤드를 일반 대입으로 연결하고 __llist_add는 그것을 사용합니다. 이중 밑줄 버전에는 CAS가 없어 외부 직렬화나 단독 접근 전제가 필요합니다. 원자 버전과 단순 이름 차이로만 이해하면 안 됩니다.

deep_dive.title: 전체 분리
deep_dive.text: llist_del_all은 xchg(&head->first,NULL)로 헤드를 원자적으로 비우고 이전 체인을 반환합니다. __llist_del_all은 일반 읽기와 쓰기만 수행합니다. 둘 다 노드를 free하지 않습니다. 단일 노드를 차례로 앞에 넣었다면 반환 순서는 최근 삽입부터이며 reverse_order로 뒤집어 오래된 순서를 만들 수 있습니다. 배치 안의 순서는 생산자가 연결한 순서입니다.

deep_dive.title: 단일 삭제와 표식 복구
deep_dive.text: llist_del_first는 외부 구현 선언이고 del_first_init은 결과가 비NULL일 때 자기참조 표식으로 바꿉니다. del_first_this와 reverse_order도 외부 선언입니다. 문서의 llist_init_node라는 철자와 달리 실제 wrapper가 호출하는 이름은 init_llist_node입니다. 이름보다 실행 코드를 기준으로 확인합니다.

deep_dive.title: CS와 동기화 범위
deep_dive.text: 다중 생산자·소비자 역할, 원자 교환과 CAS의 차이, 분리된 작업 묶음의 처리, 침입형 연결 노드, 상태 표식과 실제 소속의 차이를 학습합니다. NMI 사용은 NMI-safe cmpxchg 아키텍처 조건을 지켜야 하고 lock-less가 모든 실행 문맥에서 wait-free라는 보장은 아닙니다.

questions.explanation: NULL은 체인의 마지막 노드에도 쓰이므로 off-list를 구별하기 위해 자기참조를 사용합니다.

questions.prompt: del_all로 분리한 노드는 on_list가 반드시 false인가?
options: 그렇다. 모든 노드 표식을 자동 초기화한다
아니다. 각 next를 자기참조로 바꾸지 않는다
questions.explanation: del_all은 헤드 포인터만 교환합니다. 노드별 next는 원래 체인 연결을 유지합니다.
이중 밑줄 버전은 잠금 없는 동시 삽입 구현을 호출하지 않습니다. 사용 문맥의 별도 보호가 필요합니다.

questions.prompt: 빈 리스트 검사 후 삽입이 발생하지 않았다고 단정할 수 있는가?
options: 없다. 관측 뒤 다른 생산자가 삽입할 수 있다
questions.explanation: READ_ONCE는 잠금이나 소유권 획득이 아닙니다. 헤더도 최신성·정확성을 보장하지 않는 빠른 검사라고 설명합니다.

concepts.text: 아래 전체 해설과 원본을 함께 읽고 선언·데이터·함수·메타데이터를 구분합니다.

practice.expected: 계산 단계와 경계 조건은 파일 전체 해설과 문제별 풀이에 제시되어 있습니다. CRC 묶음의 표 전체 검산은 tests/test_crc_file_lessons.py로 재현하며 일반 파일은 명시된 소스 분기와 대조합니다.

technical_original.annotated:
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only */
#ifndef LLIST_H
#define LLIST_H
/*
 * Lock-less NULL terminated single linked list
 *
 * Cases where locking is not needed:
 * If there are multiple producers and multiple consumers, llist_add can be
 * used in producers and llist_del_all can be used in consumers simultaneously
 * without locking. Also a single consumer can use llist_del_first while
 * multiple producers simultaneously use llist_add, without any locking.
 *
 * Cases where locking is needed:
 * If we have multiple consumers with llist_del_first used in one consumer, and
 * llist_del_first or llist_del_all used in other consumers, then a lock is
 * needed.  This is because llist_del_first depends on list->first->next not
 * changing, but without lock protection, there's no way to be sure about that
 * if a preemption happens in the middle of the delete operation and on being
 * preempted back, the list->first is the same as before causing the cmpxchg in
 * llist_del_first to succeed. For example, while a llist_del_first operation
 * is in progress in one consumer, then a llist_del_first, llist_add,
 * llist_add (or llist_del_all, llist_add, llist_add) sequence in another
 * consumer may cause violations.
 *
 * This can be summarized as follows:
 *
 *           |   add    | del_first |  del_all
 * add       |    -     |     -     |     -
 * del_first |          |     L     |     L
 * del_all   |          |           |     -
 *
 * Where, a particular row's operation can happen concurrently with a column's
 * operation, with "-" being no lock needed, while "L" being lock is needed.
 *
 * The list entries deleted via llist_del_all can be traversed with
 * traversing function such as llist_for_each etc.  But the list
 * entries can not be traversed safely before deleted from the list.
 * The order of deleted entries is from the newest to the oldest added
 * one.  If you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you
 * must reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 *
 * The basic atomic operation of this list is cmpxchg on long.  On
 * architectures that don't have NMI-safe cmpxchg implementation, the
 * list can NOT be used in NMI handlers.  So code that uses the list in
 * an NMI handler should depend on CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_NMI_SAFE_CMPXCHG.
 *
 * Copyright 2010,2011 Intel Corp.
 *   Author: Huang Ying <ying.huang@intel.com>
 */

#include <linux/atomic.h>
#include <linux/container_of.h>
#include <linux/stddef.h>
#include <linux/types.h>

struct llist_head {
	struct llist_node *first;
};

struct llist_node {
	struct llist_node *next;
};

#define LLIST_HEAD_INIT(name)	{ NULL }
#define LLIST_HEAD(name)	struct llist_head name = LLIST_HEAD_INIT(name)

/**
 * init_llist_head - initialize lock-less list head
 * @head:	the head for your lock-less list
 */
static inline void init_llist_head(struct llist_head *list)
{
	list->first = NULL;
}

/**
 * init_llist_node - initialize lock-less list node
 * @node:	the node to be initialised
 *
 * In cases where there is a need to test if a node is on
 * a list or not, this initialises the node to clearly
 * not be on any list.
 */
static inline void init_llist_node(struct llist_node *node)
{
	node->next = node;
}

/**
 * llist_on_list - test if a lock-list list node is on a list
 * @node:	the node to test
 *
 * When a node is on a list the ->next pointer will be NULL or
 * some other node.  It can never point to itself.  We use that
 * in init_llist_node() to record that a node is not on any list,
 * and here to test whether it is on any list.
 */
static inline bool llist_on_list(const struct llist_node *node)
{
	return node->next != node;
}

/**
 * llist_entry - get the struct of this entry
 * @ptr:	the &struct llist_node pointer.
 * @type:	the type of the struct this is embedded in.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node within the struct.
 */
#define llist_entry(ptr, type, member)		\
	container_of(ptr, type, member)

/**
 * member_address_is_nonnull - check whether the member address is not NULL
 * @ptr:	the object pointer (struct type * that contains the llist_node)
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node within the struct.
 *
 * This macro is conceptually the same as
 *	&ptr->member != NULL
 * but it works around the fact that compilers can decide that taking a member
 * address is never a NULL pointer.
 *
 * Real objects that start at a high address and have a member at NULL are
 * unlikely to exist, but such pointers may be returned e.g. by the
 * container_of() macro.
 */
#define member_address_is_nonnull(ptr, member)	\
	((uintptr_t)(ptr) + offsetof(typeof(*(ptr)), member) != 0)

/**
 * llist_for_each - iterate over some deleted entries of a lock-less list
 * @pos:	the &struct llist_node to use as a loop cursor
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being deleted from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each(pos, node)			\
	for ((pos) = (node); pos; (pos) = (pos)->next)

/**
 * llist_for_each_safe - iterate over some deleted entries of a lock-less list
 *			 safe against removal of list entry
 * @pos:	the &struct llist_node to use as a loop cursor
 * @n:		another &struct llist_node to use as temporary storage
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being deleted from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_safe(pos, n, node)			\
	for ((pos) = (node); (pos) && ((n) = (pos)->next, true); (pos) = (n))

/**
 * llist_for_each_entry - iterate over some deleted entries of lock-less list of given type
 * @pos:	the type * to use as a loop cursor.
 * @node:	the fist entry of deleted list entries.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node with the struct.
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being removed from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_entry(pos, node, member)				\
	for ((pos) = llist_entry((node), typeof(*(pos)), member);	\
	     member_address_is_nonnull(pos, member);			\
	     (pos) = llist_entry((pos)->member.next, typeof(*(pos)), member))

/**
 * llist_for_each_entry_safe - iterate over some deleted entries of lock-less list of given type
 *			       safe against removal of list entry
 * @pos:	the type * to use as a loop cursor.
 * @n:		another type * to use as temporary storage
 * @node:	the first entry of deleted list entries.
 * @member:	the name of the llist_node with the struct.
 *
 * In general, some entries of the lock-less list can be traversed
 * safely only after being removed from list, so start with an entry
 * instead of list head.
 *
 * If being used on entries deleted from lock-less list directly, the
 * traverse order is from the newest to the oldest added entry.  If
 * you want to traverse from the oldest to the newest, you must
 * reverse the order by yourself before traversing.
 */
#define llist_for_each_entry_safe(pos, n, node, member)			       \
	for (pos = llist_entry((node), typeof(*pos), member);		       \
	     member_address_is_nonnull(pos, member) &&			       \
	        (n = llist_entry(pos->member.next, typeof(*n), member), true); \
	     pos = n)

/**
 * llist_empty - tests whether a lock-less list is empty
 * @head:	the list to test
 *
 * Not guaranteed to be accurate or up to date.  Just a quick way to
 * test whether the list is empty without deleting something from the
 * list.
 */
static inline bool llist_empty(const struct llist_head *head)
{
	return READ_ONCE(head->first) == NULL;
}

static inline struct llist_node *llist_next(struct llist_node *node)
{
	return node->next;
}

extern bool llist_add_batch(struct llist_node *new_first,
			    struct llist_node *new_last,
			    struct llist_head *head);

static inline bool __llist_add_batch(struct llist_node *new_first,
				     struct llist_node *new_last,
				     struct llist_head *head)
{
	new_last->next = head->first;
	head->first = new_first;
	return new_last->next == NULL;
}

/**
 * llist_add - add a new entry
 * @new:	new entry to be added
 * @head:	the head for your lock-less list
 *
 * Returns true if the list was empty prior to adding this entry.
 */
static inline bool llist_add(struct llist_node *new, struct llist_head *head)
{
	return llist_add_batch(new, new, head);
}

static inline bool __llist_add(struct llist_node *new, struct llist_head *head)
{
	return __llist_add_batch(new, new, head);
}

/**
 * llist_del_all - delete all entries from lock-less list
 * @head:	the head of lock-less list to delete all entries
 *
 * If list is empty, return NULL, otherwise, delete all entries and
 * return the pointer to the first entry.  The order of entries
 * deleted is from the newest to the oldest added one.
 */
static inline struct llist_node *llist_del_all(struct llist_head *head)
{
	return xchg(&head->first, NULL);
}

static inline struct llist_node *__llist_del_all(struct llist_head *head)
{
	struct llist_node *first = head->first;

	head->first = NULL;
	return first;
}

extern struct llist_node *llist_del_first(struct llist_head *head);

/**
 * llist_del_first_init - delete first entry from lock-list and mark is as being off-list
 * @head:	the head of lock-less list to delete from.
 *
 * This behave the same as llist_del_first() except that llist_init_node() is called
 * on the returned node so that llist_on_list() will report false for the node.
 */
static inline struct llist_node *llist_del_first_init(struct llist_head *head)
{
	struct llist_node *n = llist_del_first(head);

	if (n)
		init_llist_node(n);
	return n;
}

extern bool llist_del_first_this(struct llist_head *head,
				 struct llist_node *this);

struct llist_node *llist_reverse_order(struct llist_node *head);

#endif /* LLIST_H */
